topic: Lidar session data duplication and storage
summary_markdown:
The discussion focused on identifying potential issues with Lidar 2D session data, specifically the detection of duplicate sessions being sent to the system. It was noted that this duplication could originate either from the Lidar side or the processing pipeline.

Regarding data integrity, it was discussed whether the current process handles duplicates (it currently does not explicitly filter them but can be modified to collapse/deduplicate if necessary). A suggestion was made to implement a unique index on timestamps to prevent such issues.

Separately, the team confirmed that 'zero sessions' are counted. Finally, a proposal was made for improved data capture: instead of writing offline maps, it was suggested to send only one frame per minute to S3. This method aims to provide better visibility into unusual traffic spikes.
decisions: The system needs to address the issue of duplicate Lidar session records.
A unique index on timestamps should be considered for data integrity.
action_items: Someone will calculate the required storage/traffic volume for sending one frame per minute to S3.
The team needs to confirm how to retrieve vehicle counts for a specific period from the database.
